findings.title: Rejected devices remain cached and can bypass the limit
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` caches the device ID before calling the store. When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, this error is propagated but the cache entry is not removed. The next request with the same ID hits the cache, skips the store check, and authenticates successfully for the cache lifetime, bypassing the configured device limit.

findings.title: Device count and insert are not atomic
findings.body: The limit check counts devices in a separate operation from the subsequent insert. Concurrent requests for distinct devices can all observe a count below the limit and then all insert successfully, exceeding the configured limit; this can also happen across Grafana instances. Enforce capacity atomically rather than relying on this count-then-insert sequence.

findings.title: A no-op MySQL update is treated as a limit rejection
findings.body: MySQL normally reports only changed rows from `RowsAffected`. At the limit, updating an existing device can leave every field unchanged—for example, when another Grafana instance handles the same device in the same second and the IP and user agent match, given the database's second-level timestamp precision. In that case this check returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and rejects a device that should be allowed.

findings.title: Document the new anonymous device-limit setting
findings.body: This adds `auth.anonymous.device_limit` as a configurable setting, but the PR does not update the default configuration or configuration documentation. Operators have no documented way to discover the setting or understand its default and behavior, making the feature difficult to configure correctly.
